Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The West Indies are in a huddle for some last-minute pep talk, and now they spread out to take their respective field positions. Shubman Gill and Yashasvi Jaiswal are the two openers for India. Obed McCoy to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Righ then, West Indies have posted a decent total but they know that they should have scored way more looking at the pitch. Their bowlers now have their task cut out to defend this one. India has a lot of batting firepower in their ranks and will be hopeful that they deliver to gun this total down and level the series. Join us in a bit to see how the chase unfolds.

Shai Hope is down for a quick chat. He says that they started well but didn't do justice in the middle overs and then applauds Shimron Hetmyer for the way he batted and they finished well. Mentions that he tries to stay positive against the bowlers and a couple of partnerships were crucial for them. Adds that getting the opportunity to play is a big thing and hopes that his contribution gives them the win.

India, on the other hand, can take a lot of positives from their bowling effort. After struggling a bit initially, Arshdeep Singh started things off by getting rid of both the openers. Kuldeep Yadav followed it with a fantastic opening over where he sent both Pooran and Powell packing which gave the momentum to the visitors. They did not give too many loose balls to the hosts and controlled the game for most parts. Mukesh Kumar was once again brilliant with his yorkers and got one wicket while Yuzvendra Chahal who was expensive chipped in with one as well, and Axar Patel picked up one too. However, Arshdeep Singh ended up three wickets but gave a few too many in the last over which he will not be happy about.

West Indies got off to a decent start with Kyle Mayers playing a few lusty blows before getting out in the second over. Brandon King and Shai Hope who came in the side for Johnson Charles then steadied things for a bit, but they suffered a mini collapse as they went from 54-1 to 57-4 losing both Nicholas Pooran and Rovman Powell in the process. After that, Shimron Hetmyer and Hope tried to control things with a 49-run stand, but once the latter was dismissed for 45 off just 29 balls, it went downhill for the hosts. However, Hettie did not give his wicket away and continued to find those crucial boundaries in the middle. He registered an excellent fifty and took the attack to India at the fag end of the innings while some good blows from Akeal Hosein and Odean Smith can help them take that momentum into their bowling now.

A fine all-round bowling show from India! They were right on point with their line and lengths on a wicket that didn't offer much to the bowlers and restricted West Indies to 178. There were a couple of individual performers for the hosts, most notably the gritty half-century from Shimron Hetmyer, but India will still be the happier side going into the break.

SIX! BANG! Odean Smith flexes his muscles and finishes the innings off in style. On a good length outside off, Smith just hangs deep in his crease and thumps it well over the long off fence for a biggie. West Indies get 17 runs off the final over and finish with 178/8.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin! The umpires make their way out to the middle as the Indian players are seen in a huddle before taking their places on the field. The pair of Kyle Mayers and Brandon King will open the innings for West Indies. It will be spin to get proceedings underway as Axar Patel has been handed the new ball. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Ian Bishop is pitchside and says that the boundaries are 67 meters and 65 meters square with the straight boundaries being 74 meters and says that there is a breeze blowing across. Shakera Selman joins him and says that there is a sheen on the pitch which means the ball will slide on and the batters will enjoy it. Adds that the average score is around 175 and a score of 180 plus is on the cards but does mention that later in the day, it just slows up a touch.

Hardik Pandya, the skipper of India says that they would have batted first as well. Adds that it looks like a good track and it would not change much. Tells that the boys turned up well in the last game, especially SKY and Tilak Varma, and the hunger was there as everyone chipped in at all departments. Mentions that their spinners have that knack for picking wickets and they try to keep things simple but don't let the intensity drop out there. Informs they are unchanged.

Rovman Powell, the captain of West Indies says that they will bat first as it looks like a good surface and want to put runs on the board. Adds that it is an opportunity for them to get a series win against a big team. Mentions that Jason Holder is back in and there are a couple of other changes as well. Tells that you need to be on your game in all three departments and control what you can control.

India (Unchanged Playing XI) - Shubman Gill, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Suryakumar Yadav, Tilak Varma, Hardik Pandya (C), Sanju Samson (WK), Axar Patel, Arshdeep Singh, Kuldeep Yadav, Yuzvendra Chahal, Mukesh Kumar.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Kyle Mayers, Brandon King, Shai Hope (In place of Johnson Charles), Nicholas Pooran (WK), Rovman Powell (C), Shimron Hetmyer, Romario Shepherd, Jason Holder (In place of Roston Chase), Odean Smith (In place of Alzarri Joseph), Akeal Hosein, Obed McCoy.
TOSS - The coin lands in favour of Rovman Powell and West Indies have elected to BAT first.

India, on the other hand, finally managed to get a win in this series. SKY was back to his best, but the struggles for Shubman Gill continued and Yashasvi Jaiswal also couldn't do much on his debut. They could think about getting Ishan Kishan in for one of them. However, the most significant positive has been Tilak Varma who grabbed his opportunity with both hands scoring a fifty in the second game while just missing out on it in the previous match as Hardik Pandya finished things off before Verma got the chance to reach that milestone. Kuldeep Yadav has been the most impressive bowler while Arshdeep Singh and Mukesh Kumar have bowled well in the Powerplay as well as at the death. They will be confident and look to continue the winning momentum to level the series. Let's see who comes out on top. Toss and team news in a bit.

West Indies would need a better performance than the last game. Their openers need to improve the scoring rate to release some burden from the middle order. Another worry is the form of Johnson Charles at number 3 but he has a good record at this ground and will look for a change in fortunes. However, the most important player for them is Nicholas Pooran who is in sublime form and is also the highest-run scorer against India in this format. Alzarri Joseph will be the key in the bowling department along with Romario Shepherd. Obed McCoy and Roston Chase could be useful if the wicket is slow. Windies will hope that everything falls in place and they get the win here.

Hello and a warm welcome folks! The action for the last two matches in this T20I series between India and West Indies has moved to Central Broward Regional Park in Florida, U.S.A. India bounced back well in the last game to make it 2-1 and will hope to level it in this game to take it to a decider while Windies will want to avoid any more hiccups and seal it with a victory.
... MATCH DAY ...

The caravan has arrived on the coasts of the United States of America for the last two games of what has been a really long tour for the Indians. We now arrive at the Central Broward Regional Park Stadium Turf Ground in Lauderhill in the coastal state of Florida for the 4th T20I in this 5-match series between India and West Indies. The series is nicely poised as West Indies got off to a great start winning the first two games and putting pressure on a formidable Indian side. The Men in Blue did make an impressive comeback in the last match but still trail 2-1 in the series and will be hoping to come on level terms in this fixture. It was an impressive win for the visitors as Suryakumar Yadav played a scintillating knock and Tilak Varma continued his good form in the series by taking his side to a comfortable 7-wicket win. He has made the selectors back in India stand up and take notice which puts him in serious contention for the World Cup later this year. The experiments with the playing XI are still on with Yashasvi Jaiswal getting his debut in the last game but could not make the most of it. Shubman Gill has been out of sorts all through the tour and will be hoping to return to form as soon as possible while Sanju Samson probably has the last few opportunities to prove his mettle. Mukesh Kumar and Arshdeep Singh have good spells but have lacked consistency which has put the pace-bowling responsibility heavily on Hardik Pandya. They have opted for three spinners in Axar Patel, Kuldeep Yadav and Yuzvendra Chahal and it will be interesting to see if one gets dropped in the last two games. West Indies have seen Nicholas Pooran and Rovman Powell contribute heavily towards a chunk of the good work done by the hosts. The openers Brandon King and Kyle Mayers have all got starts but are missing the big scores while the form of Johnson Charles is a bit of a worry. Alzarri Joseph and Romario Shepherd spearhead the pace bowling attack and Akeal Hosein had Roston Chase for help in the last game in their spin bowling unit, unlike the first two games. They will need to get their plans in order to return to winning ways and seal the series with a game in hand. The weather may have a massive role to play as there is some rain on the radar during the game but we hope that the rain gods stay away. Will India be able to level the series? Or will West Indies register an elusive series win against the visitors? We will find out soon.
